CLI client

# CLI client

Source: [MCP c1c81072](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/c1c81072057ed9a3eb40a1213eb7577651c1937b/docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/cli.mdx)

## A runnable CLI lab and its limits

For executable examples with failure interpretation, start with [the Inspector 2.12.0 lab](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/tools/inspector/). It includes a Python SDK `2.3.0` reference server, the complete smoke script, 26 previously recorded scenarios and explicit untested features. A CLI invocation runs one method on a fresh connection; several successful invocations do not establish a long-running session or UI workflow.

Task| Entry| Check before use  
---|---|---  
Scripts, CI and troubleshooting| This reference and the linked lab| Pin `@modelcontextprotocol/[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)`; separate server and Inspector arguments  
Inspect requests interactively| [Web client](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/web/)| Its backend can spawn local processes; read API-token and bind-address boundaries before exposing a port  
Import configuration| [Configuration and flags](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/configuration/)| Use read-only `--config` for someone else's file; writable `--catalog` is different; inspect stdio commands before executing them  
Sign in or recover expired credentials| [Authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/authorization/)| Check the client's callback URL, storage and non-interactive policy; keep credentials out of logs  
  
In the CLI, stdio server arguments precede `--`, and Inspector options follow it. Web / TUI use a different split, so do not copy a complete command between modes. Declare the protocol era in automation: the default `legacy` success establishes only the legacy path, `auto` can probe and fall back, and `modern` does not fall back. Strict schema failures, connection failures and a tool's `isError` are separate outcomes.

On 2026-10-30 only the subset needed here was rerun: clean stdio, pre-start banner, process exit, legacy HTTP versus modern, and 401 / 403 / 404 / HTML. Other scenarios retain the lab's previous recordings; all 26 were not rerun. Web / TUI, `mcpdo`, real OAuth, skills verification and App UI remain untested. The pinned reference below documents options; their presence does not establish a site test result.

Each CLI run connects to a server, invokes the single request you name with `--method`, prints the result, and exits. That makes it a good fit for CI pipelines, shell one-liners, and coding agents that need to verify a server change immediately.
    
    
    npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli node build/index.js --method tools/list

Running several commands against the same server, or a flow that spans one session (tasks, subscriptions, elicitation)? The [mcpdo connection client](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/mcpdo/) connects once and keeps the connection open between commands.

The examples below use the installed `mcp-inspector` binary. Without a global install, prefix each command with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` instead, as above.

## Choosing a server

The CLI accepts a positional command (stdio), a `--server-url` (HTTP/SSE), or a named server out of a catalog or config file:
    
    
    # stdio: everything positional is the command to spawn
    mcp-inspector --cli node build/index.js --method tools/list
    
    # HTTP
    mcp-inspector --cli https://api.example.com/mcp --transport http --method tools/list
    
    # From a file
    mcp-inspector --cli --config ./mcp.json --server myserver --method tools/list

When the server comes from a file, its per-server settings (headers, timeouts, OAuth, [protocol era](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/protocol-eras/), and roots) apply to the connection, resolved exactly as the TUI and web client resolve them. A `--header` flag overrides the file's headers for that run while leaving its timeouts and OAuth in place.

Later examples abbreviate whichever of these forms you use, along with its `--transport` or `--config`/`--server` flags, as `<server>`.

**The config file is the only durable way to give a run its[roots](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/client/roots/):** there is no roots flag, and the CLI has no `roots/set` method. Roots configured for a server are advertised at connect, so a server that calls `roots/list` (as `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` does, to learn its allowed directories) gets them.

See [Configuration and flags](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/configuration/) for `--catalog` vs. `--config`, the `--` separator, and the shared server-selection flags.

## Methods

`--method`| Required companions| Notes  
---|---|---  
`initialize`| None| Connect-only probe: `{serverInfo, protocolVersion, capabilities, instructions}`.  
`tools/list`| None| `--strict` turns its schema portability check into a gate (see CI gates).  
`tools/call`| `--tool-name`, plus optional `--tool-arg` / `--tool-args-json`|   
`resources/list`| None|   
`resources/read`| `--uri`|   
`resources/templates/list`| None|   
`resources/directory/read`| `--uri`, plus optional `--cursor`| One page at a time; pass back the previous page's `nextCursor`.  
`prompts/list`| None|   
`prompts/get`| `--prompt-name`, plus optional `--prompt-args`|   
`logging/setLevel`| `--log-level`| Legacy era only; modern servers opt in per request instead.  
`skills/list`| None| `--verify` checks the skills returned (see CI gates).  
`skills/get`| `--uri`| Same `--verify` option.  
`servers/list`| None| Read the catalog **without connecting** to anything.  
`servers/show`| `--server`| Same, for one entry.  
`servers/add`| `--server`, plus a positional target or `--server-url`| Write the catalog without connecting (see Editing the catalog).  
`servers/edit`| `--server`, plus what to change| Same.  
`servers/remove`| `--server`| Same.  
  
Stream- or session-only methods (`logging/tail`, for example) are rejected, since a process that exits can't hold a stream open.

### Passing arguments

`--tool-arg` takes `key=value` and **coerces** each value by JSON-parsing it when it parses, so `count=1` and `zip=10001` both send numbers. A value that is not valid JSON (`zip=012`, a bare word) is sent as a string, and a string is then converted to the type the tool's input schema declares for that property, so `zip=012` against a numeric `zip` still sends `12`:
    
    
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/call --tool-name mytool \
      --tool-arg key=value --tool-arg count=1 --tool-arg 'options={"format":"json"}'

`--tool-args-json` takes the whole argument object at once and skips the `key=value` parsing, so `{"zip":"10001"}` sends the string `"10001"` rather than a number. The schema conversion still applies to string values, so this only keeps a string a string when the schema types that property as a string (or doesn't declare it). The two flags are mutually exclusive:
    
    
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/call --tool-name mytool \
      --tool-args-json '{"zip":"10001"}'

## Output

`--format text` (the default) pretty-prints for humans. `--format json` emits a single JSON object on stdout with no banners, so the whole output pipes cleanly:
    
    
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/list --format json | jq '.result.tools[].name'

## Probing MCP Apps

`--app-info` reports whether a tool ships an [MCP App](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/extensions/apps/overview/) UI (its `ui://` resource, CSP, and permissions) **without calling the tool** , so a pipeline can decide whether it needs a browser before invoking anything:
    
    
    # One tool -> one JSON line
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/call --tool-name my_tool --app-info
    # {"hasApp":true,"toolName":"my_tool","resourceUri":"ui://...","csp":{...},"permissions":{...}}
    
    # Every tool -> NDJSON, one line each, over a single connection
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/list --app-info | jq -c 'select(.hasApp)'

Exit codes distinguish the outcomes: a tool with an app exits `0`, one with no app exits `2`, and a missing tool exits `5`, so a typo isn't mistaken for "no app". A probe failure (unreadable UI resource, malformed `resourceUri`) is reported in a `resourceError` field rather than aborting, so one bad tool never kills a whole listing.

The CLI can't render an App, so by default it doesn't advertise the MCP Apps extension at `initialize`. A server that exposes its App tools only to clients claiming App support will then look app-less (exit `2`). Add `--advertise-apps` to claim the extension for that run.

`tools/list --app-info` always emits NDJSON (one line per tool) regardless of `--format`; `--format json` reshapes only the single-tool output of `tools/call --app-info`.

## Exit codes and error envelopes

Every non-zero exit maps to a stable failure class, so a caller can branch on _why_ without scraping prose:

Code| Meaning  
---|---  
`0`| Success.  
`1`| Usage or unexpected error (the catch-all), including an unreadable secret store or OAuth state file.  
`2`| No MCP App found on the tool (`--app-info` probe).  
`3`| Server requires authentication (HTTP 401/403, or an SDK authorization error).  
`4`| Server unreachable (DNS, connection refused, timeout, `fetch failed`).  
`5`| Tool error: `tools/call` returned `isError: true`, or the tool wasn't found.  
`6`| `--strict` found an error-severity tool-schema portability problem.  
`7`| `--verify` found a skill that violates SEP-2640 (conformance, digest, or size mismatch).  
`8`| `--verify` couldn't check every skill within its read bounds.  
`9`| `--verify --require-digests` found a skill that advertises no digests.  
`10`| A `--load` run breached a `--load-max-error-rate` or `--load-max-p99` threshold. The summary is printed first, and the envelope `code` names the threshold: `load_error_rate_exceeded` or `load_p99_exceeded`.  
`11`| The server answered HTTP 429 (envelope `code` `rate_limited`). The envelope also carries `method`, plus `retryAfter` (the `Retry-After` header as sent) and `retryAfterMs` when the server sent one that parses.  
  
On any non-zero exit the CLI also writes a **single JSON line to stderr** :
    
    
    {
      "error": {
        "code": "auth_required",
        "message": "Unauthorized",
        "status": 401,
        "url": "https://api.example/mcp"
      }
    }

The envelope carries `code` and `message` always, plus `cause` (the underlying error, such as a DNS failure), `status` (the HTTP status) and `url` when known. Query-string secrets in a URL are redacted. `code` is a stable name for the failure: `auth_required`, `unreachable`, `tool_not_found`, `tool_is_error`, `no_app`, `schema_unportable`, `store_unavailable`, `oauth_state_unrecognized`, `rate_limited`, or the catch-all `error`, among others.

Because it's one line, a caller can parse it with `2>&1 | tail -1 | jq .error`.

A `tools/call` that returns `isError: true` still prints its payload, but exits `5`, so an `&&` chain doesn't proceed on a failed call.

## Authorization in scripts

By default the CLI runs the same loopback OAuth flow as the TUI: it opens a browser and waits on a localhost callback that a CI job can't complete. Two flags make non-interactive runs predictable:

  * `--stored-auth-only`: never start interactive OAuth or step-up, and never auto-open a browser. Use tokens from the shared store if present, otherwise fail immediately with `auth_required`. This is the flag CI wants.
  * `--use-stored-auth`: reuse a token that the web Inspector already obtained on this machine, refreshing it first when a refresh token is stored. It looks the token up by URL, so it requires `--server-url`.



Without either, and with no TTY on stdin or stderr, the CLI fails fast with `auth_required` rather than hanging for fifteen minutes on a callback nobody will complete.

See [Authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/authorization/) for the full flow, the web-to-CLI handoff, and `--print-handoff`.

## Recipes

### Verify a server in CI
    
    
    set -euo pipefail
    
    # Fail the build if the server can't be reached or doesn't expose the tool
    mcp-inspector --cli --config ./ci-servers.json --server my-server \
      --stored-auth-only --method tools/list --format json \
      | jq -e '.result.tools | map(.name) | index("get_weather")' > /dev/null

### CI gates

These flags turn a check into a non-zero exit, each with its own code so a job can tell the failures apart:

  * `--strict` (with `tools/list`): reports tool-schema portability problems in full on stderr (path, issue, suggested fix) and exits `6` if any is error-severity. Without it, `tools/list` prints only a one-line count. Under `--format json` the findings are folded into the output as `schemaFindings`.
  * `--verify` (with `skills/list` or `skills/get`): runs the SEP-2640 conformance and digest checks, writes one JSON report per skill on stdout, and exits `7` on a violation or `8` when the read bounds stopped it before every skill was checked. `--skill-catalog-max-skills` and `--skill-catalog-max-bytes` set those bounds.
  * `--require-digests` (with `--verify`): exits `9` for a skill that advertises no digests, instead of reporting it as unverifiable and exiting `0`.
  * `--load-max-error-rate <fraction>` and `--load-max-p99 <ms>` (with `--load`): turn a load run into a gate. The run prints its summary, then exits `10` when the share of failed calls is above the fraction (`0` to `1`, so `0` fails on any failed call), when the p99 latency is above the given milliseconds, or when no call completed. `--load` (with `tools/call --tool-name`) calls the tool repeatedly and concurrently and prints a latency and error-rate summary instead of a result, bounded by `--load-duration <sec>` (default `10` when `--load-requests` is not set) and `--load-requests <n>`, with in-flight calls still finishing. `--load-concurrency <n>` (default `10`) caps the calls in flight, `--load-connections <n>` (default `1`, at most `--load-concurrency`, HTTP and SSE servers only) spreads them over independent sessions opened before timing starts, and `--load-rate <n>` (default unlimited) caps the calls started per second.


    
    
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/list --strict > /dev/null
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method skills/list --verify --require-digests
    mcp-inspector --cli <server> --method tools/call --tool-name get_weather --load --load-requests 200 --load-max-p99 500

### Branch on the failure class
    
    
    if out=$(mcp-inspector --cli "$URL" --transport http --method tools/list 2>err.json); then
      echo "$out"
    else
      case $? in
        3) echo "needs auth: run the web inspector once to sign in" ;;
        4) echo "server unreachable" ;;
        *) jq .error < err.json ;;
      esac
    fi

### Smoke-test every tool that has a UI
    
    
    mcp-inspector --cli "$URL" --transport http --method tools/list --app-info \
      | jq -r 'select(.hasApp) | .toolName'

### Inspect a catalog without connecting
    
    
    mcp-inspector --cli --catalog ~/.mcp-inspector/mcp.json --method servers/list
    mcp-inspector --cli --catalog ~/.mcp-inspector/mcp.json --method servers/show --server my-server

`servers/show` redacts secret-bearing fields (`env` values, sensitive headers, OAuth client secrets), but it does **not** scrub credentials embedded in a server `url` (userinfo or query tokens) or in stdio `args`. Treat raw URL and `detail` fields as sensitive before pasting them into an issue.

### Editing the catalog

`servers/add`, `servers/edit`, and `servers/remove` write the catalog without connecting to anything. They go through the same code as the web client's server list, so `env` values and client secrets land in the [secret store](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/configuration/#where-secrets-are-stored) exactly as they would from the UI, and a running web client picks up the change.
    
    
    # Add: the positional target or --server-url describes the entry, not a server to connect to
    mcp-inspector --cli node build/index.js -e API_KEY=secret --method servers/add --server my-server
    
    # Edit: change the target, -e, --cwd, --header, or --protocol-era, or rename it
    mcp-inspector --cli --method servers/edit --server my-server --rename my-renamed-server
    
    # Remove the entry and its stored secrets
    mcp-inspector --cli --method servers/remove --server my-renamed-server

Only the writable catalog (`--catalog`, `MCP_CATALOG_PATH`, or the default) can be written; `--config` is refused. With an in-memory secret store, a write that supplies `-e` values (and a `--rename`) is refused, since the secrets would be lost when the run exits.

## Proxies

Connections to remote HTTP/SSE servers honor the conventional proxy variables: `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` (and their lowercase forms) select the proxy and `NO_PROXY` exempts hosts. No Inspector-specific flag is needed, and the proxy agent is loaded lazily, so runs without a proxy pay nothing. The same applies to the web client's backend.

MCP Clients: What Each One Supports and How to Confirm What a Client Declares

# MCP Clients: What Each One Supports and How to Confirm What a Client Declares

Vendor documentation and capability measurements here are dated **2026-10-26** , not a continuously certified compatibility list. Rerun the embedded probe after upgrading a client. Distinguish specification capabilities, vendor wording and observed declarations; a declaration alone does not validate UI or tool execution.

Before a server relies on a client, confirm three things: which tools, resources and prompts the client puts in front of its users; whether it answers server-initiated roots, sampling and elicitation requests; and which protocol revision it speaks. The tables list only capabilities stated by each vendor; an empty cell means the page is silent. To confirm what the client in front of you actually declares, run the probe server in section 5.

For the lifecycle and the messages that these declarations take part in, read [the learning path](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/learning-path/) and [MCP architecture](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/learn/architecture/). For what a server offers, read [tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/tools/), [resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/) and [prompts](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/).

## 1\. What "supports MCP" can mean

Three different things hide behind the phrase. Only the second and third are visible in the protocol.

Layer| What the client does| Where it is declared| How a server finds out  
---|---|---|---  
Primitives| Calls `tools/list`, `resources/list` and `prompts/list` and shows or uses the results| Nowhere: tools, resources and prompts are server capabilities, and a client has no capability named after them| By the calls that arrive, or from the vendor's documentation  
Client capabilities| Answers requests that the server starts: `roots/list`, sampling, elicitation (and `tasks` or `extensions` in some revisions)| `ClientCapabilities`: in `initialize` up to 2025-11-25, in the `_meta` of every request in 2026-07-28| By reading the declaration (section 4)  
Revision| Speaks one or more protocol revisions| The `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, and `initialize` or `server/discover`| From the first requests of a connection (section 6)  
  
The rule that makes the declaration worth reading: in 2025-11-25 both sides "Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated", and in 2026-07-28 a server "MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared". If it needs one, it returns a `MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError` (`-32021`) with HTTP status 400. Because tools, resources and prompts carry no declaration, the matrix in section 2 rests on what vendors write, and section 5 shows how to measure the rest.

## 2\. What each vendor's page says

A ✓ means that the vendor's own documentation states the feature; the number in brackets is the row of the wording table in section 3. An empty cell means the page does not say. It does not mean the client lacks the feature. Clients that were previously listed without a source are not carried over.

Client| Tools| Resources| Prompts| Roots| Sampling| Elicitation| Revision named  
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---  
Claude Code| ✓ (1)| ✓ (2)| ✓ (3)| ✓ (4)| | ✓ (5)| 2026-07-28 (6)  
Cursor| ✓ (7)| ✓ (8)| ✓ (9)| ✓ (10)| | ✓ (11)|   
VS Code| ✓ (12)| ✓ (13)| ✓ (14)| ✓ (15)| ✓ (16)| ✓ (17)|   
Zed| ✓ (18)| | ✓ (18)| | | |   
Gemini CLI| ✓ (19)| ✓ (20)| ✓ (21)| | | |   
  
  * All five clients state tools. Zed alone leaves resources empty: its page names "Tools and Prompts" only (18).
  * Sampling is stated by VS Code only (16). Section 6 shows that Claude Code 2.1.292 does not declare it either, which agrees with its empty cell.
  * Roots and elicitation are stated together by Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code, and by nobody else in this table.
  * Only Claude Code names a protocol revision, 2026-07-28 (6). For the others the page is silent, so read what they send (section 6).

## 4\. What a client declares, revision by revision

`ClientCapabilities` is the one place where a client says what it will answer. The table is computed from `schema/<revision>/schema.json` at the pinned commit; ✓ lists the sub-fields that the revision's schema defines, and — means the capability does not exist in that revision.

Capability| 2024-11-05| 2025-03-26| 2025-06-18| 2025-11-25| 2026-07-28  
---|---|---|---|---|---  
`roots`| ✓ (`listChanged`)| ✓ (`listChanged`)| ✓ (`listChanged`)| ✓ (`listChanged`)| ✓  
`sampling`| ✓| ✓| ✓| ✓ (`context`, `tools`)| ✓ (`context`, `tools`)  
`elicitation`| —| —| ✓| ✓ (`form`, `url`)| ✓ (`form`, `url`)  
`tasks`| —| —| —| ✓ (`cancel`, `list`, `requests`)| —  
`extensions`| —| —| —| —| ✓  
`experimental`| ✓| ✓| ✓| ✓| ✓  
  
  * **Where it travels.** Up to 2025-11-25 the client declares once, in `initialize`. In 2026-07-28 it puts the declaration in `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` on every request, and a client that supports roots "MUST declare the `roots` capability" there on each request. There is no `initialize` in that revision; see [the learning path](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/learning-path/).
  * **Elicitation modes.** For backward compatibility an empty `elicitation` object means form mode only. A server MUST NOT send an elicitation request in a mode the client has not declared (2025-11-25).
  * **Sampling sub-capabilities (2025-11-25).** A server MUST NOT send tool-enabled sampling requests unless the client declared `sampling.tools`, and SHOULD NOT use `includeContext` values `thisServer` or `allServers` unless it declared `sampling.context`.
  * **Roots in 2026-07-28.** The request is delivered inside an `InputRequiredResult`, in `inputRequests`. The schema now defines `roots` as an object without fields.
  * **`tasks`** is a client capability in 2025-11-25 only. In 2026-07-28 it is no longer part of the core protocol.
  * **Deprecation (2026-07-28).** Roots and sampling are deprecated by SEP-2577. They remain in the specification, but new implementations SHOULD NOT adopt them; elicitation is not deprecated. Design a new server so that it also works with a client that declares neither roots nor sampling.



## 5\. A probe server that records the declaration

The probe is a standard-library HTTP server. It answers just enough protocol for a client to connect, offers empty tool, resource and prompt lists so that a client has a reason to ask for them, and prints one JSON line per request: the method, the protocol revision, the client's name and version, and the capabilities it declares. It issues no session id, so run one client at a time.
    
    
    python3 client_probe_server.py --era modern --port 8240   # server/discover answered, initialize refused
    python3 client_probe_server.py --era legacy --port 8240   # initialize answered, server/discover refused

Point the client at `http://127.0.0.1:8240/mcp` by adding it as a remote HTTP server in the client's own MCP settings. For Claude Code that is `claude mcp add --transport http probe http://127.0.0.1:8240/mcp`. A client that speaks both eras probes `server/discover` first and falls back to `initialize`, so the legacy probe shows the legacy declaration of any such client; a legacy-only client is refused by the modern probe, which tells you its era. A hosted client cannot reach `127.0.0.1`; use a tunnel for it, and stop the probe when you are done.

**client_probe_server.py**
    
    
     #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """Probe MCP server: record what a connecting client says about itself and which list methods it calls.
    
    Usage: client_probe_server.py [--era modern|legacy] [--port 8240]
    Point a client at http://127.0.0.1:8240/mcp. Every POST prints one JSON line:
      method, protocol (the MCP-Protocol-Version header, or the version the client offers in `initialize`),
      version (the protocolVersion in the `_meta` of a modern request), client (name and version),
      capabilities (what the client declares: roots, sampling, elicitation, ...).
    `--era modern` answers `server/discover` (revision 2026-07-28; a client names itself in the `_meta` of every
    request) and refuses `initialize`. `--era legacy` refuses `server/discover` and answers `initialize` (a client names
    itself once, in the handshake). The server offers empty tool, resource and prompt lists, so a client that wants
    any of the three has a reason to ask. Standard library only.
    """
    import argparse
    import json
    import sys
    from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
    
    PREFIX = "io.modelcontextprotocol/"
    MODERN = "2026-07-28"
    LEGACY = ["2025-11-25", "2025-06-18", "2025-03-26", "2024-11-05"]
    CAPABILITIES = {"tools": {}, "resources": {}, "prompts": {}}
    LISTS = {"tools/list": "tools", "resources/list": "resources", "prompts/list": "prompts"}
    
    
    def make_handler(era, log):
        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args):  # keep stdout for the records
                pass
    
            def reply(self, status, body=None):
                data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else b""
                self.send_response(status)
                if body is not None:
                    self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)
    
            def do_GET(self):  # no server-initiated stream: the spec allows 405
                self.reply(405)
    
            do_DELETE = do_GET
    
            def do_POST(self):
                try:
                    msg = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))))
                    method, params = msg["method"], msg.get("params") or {}
                except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                    return self.reply(400, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": None, "error": {"code": -32700, "message": "bad request"}})
                meta = params.get("_meta") or {}
                entry = {"method": method, "protocol": self.headers.get("MCP-Protocol-Version") or params.get("protocolVersion"),
                         "version": meta.get(PREFIX + "protocolVersion"),
                         "client": meta.get(PREFIX + "clientInfo") or params.get("clientInfo"),
                         "capabilities": meta.get(PREFIX + "clientCapabilities", params.get("capabilities"))}
                log({k: v for k, v in entry.items() if v is not None})
                if "id" not in msg:  # a notification gets no body
                    return self.reply(202)
                result, error = None, None
                if method == "server/discover" and era == "modern":
                    result = {"resultType": "complete", "supportedVersions": [MODERN], "capabilities": CAPABILITIES,
                              "ttlMs": 0, "cacheScope": "private"}
                elif method == "initialize" and era == "legacy":
                    offered = params.get("protocolVersion")
                    result = {"protocolVersion": offered if offered in LEGACY else LEGACY[0], "capabilities": CAPABILITIES,
                              "serverInfo": {"name": "client-probe", "version": "1"}}
                elif method in LISTS:
                    result = {LISTS[method]: []}
                    if era == "modern":
                        result.update(resultType="complete", ttlMs=0, cacheScope="private")
                else:
                    error = {"code": -32601, "message": "Method not found: %s" % method}
                body = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"]}
                body.update({"error": error} if error else {"result": result})
                self.reply(200, body)
    
        return Handler
    
    
    def summarize(record):
        """One readable line per record: method, protocol, client, and the capability names it declares."""
        parts = ["%-26s" % record["method"], "protocol=%s" % record.get("protocol")]
        client = record.get("client")
        if client:
            parts.append("client=%s/%s" % (client.get("name"), client.get("version")))
        if "capabilities" in record:
            parts.append("declares=%s" % (sorted(record["capabilities"]) or "nothing"))
        return "  " + " ".join(parts).rstrip()
    
    
    def serve(era, port, log):
        return ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), make_handler(era, log))
    
    
    def main():
        ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        ap.add_argument("--era", choices=["modern", "legacy"], default="modern")
        ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8240)
        args = ap.parse_args()
        server = serve(args.era, args.port, lambda e: print(json.dumps(e, sort_keys=True), flush=True))
        print("probe (%s era) on http://127.0.0.1:%d/mcp" % (args.era, args.port), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        try:
            server.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

## 6\. Run results

### The official Python SDK

`probe_runs.py` starts the probe inside the script and connects `mcp.client.Client` of the official SDK to it four times: modern and legacy probe, each without callbacks and with callbacks for sampling, roots and elicitation. The three list calls are issued by the script; a real client issues its own.

Probe server| Client callbacks| Requests, in order| Declared  
---|---|---|---  
`modern`| none| `server/discover` → `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`| nothing  
`modern`| `sampling`, `roots`, `elicitation`| `server/discover` → `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`| `elicitation`, `roots`, `sampling`  
`legacy`| none| `server/discover` → `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`| nothing  
`legacy`| `sampling`, `roots`, `elicitation`| `server/discover` → `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`| `elicitation`, `roots`, `sampling`  
  
  * The SDK declares what its callbacks allow and nothing else. "The SDK supports sampling" therefore means that the application passed a sampling callback.
  * Against the legacy probe the SDK sends `server/discover`, gets a refusal, and then sends `initialize` with 2025-11-25. Its mode `auto` does this on purpose. A refused `server/discover` is normal in the legacy era and no sign of failure.
  * Its default `clientInfo` is `mcp/0.1.0`. A product built on the SDK may therefore not be identifiable by name alone.

**probe_runs.py**
    
    
     #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """Connect the official Python SDK client (mcp==2.3.0) to the probe server in four configurations and print what
    the probe recorded. The list calls are issued by this script; a real client issues its own, and that is what you read.
    
    Usage: probe_runs.py      Exit code 0 = every run recorded what its configuration implies, 1 = it did not.
    """
    import asyncio
    import sys
    import threading
    
    from mcp import types
    from mcp.client import Client
    
    import client_probe_server as probe
    
    PORT = 8241
    
    
    async def no_sampling(context, params):
        return types.ErrorData(code=-32601, message="not used in this run")
    
    
    async def no_roots(context):
        return types.ErrorData(code=-32601, message="not used in this run")
    
    
    async def no_elicitation(context, params):
        return types.ErrorData(code=-32601, message="not used in this run")
    
    
    def run(era, callbacks):
        records = []
        server = probe.serve(era, PORT, records.append)
        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        kwargs = {"sampling_callback": no_sampling, "list_roots_callback": no_roots,
                  "elicitation_callback": no_elicitation} if callbacks else {}
    
        async def drive():
            async with Client("http://127.0.0.1:%d/mcp" % PORT, **kwargs) as client:
                await client.list_tools()
                await client.list_resources()
                await client.list_prompts()
    
        try:
            asyncio.run(drive())
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()
            thread.join()
        return records
    
    
    def main():
        failed = 0
        for era in ("modern", "legacy"):
            for callbacks in (False, True):
                records = run(era, callbacks)
                print("run: era=%s callbacks=%s" % (era, "sampling,roots,elicitation" if callbacks else "none"))
                for record in records:
                    print(probe.summarize(record))
                methods = [r["method"] for r in records]
                declared = [r for r in records if "capabilities" in r]
                wanted = ["elicitation", "roots", "sampling"] if callbacks else []
                ok = (methods[:1] == ["server/discover"]  # the SDK always probes first
                      and ("initialize" in methods) == (era == "legacy")  # only a legacy server gets the handshake
                      and [m for m in methods if m.endswith("/list")] == ["tools/list", "resources/list", "prompts/list"]
                      and bool(declared) and all(sorted(r["capabilities"]) == wanted for r in declared))
                print("  check: %s" % ("as configured" if ok else "NOT as configured"))
                failed += 0 if ok else 1
        return 1 if failed else 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        sys.exit(main())

### Claude Code 2.1.292

`claude_code_probe.py` adds the probe to the real `claude` CLI, runs `claude mcp list` (its health check) and prints what arrived. `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` point at a throw-away directory, so your own configuration is neither read nor changed. Measured on macOS on 2026-10-26.

Probe server| `claude mcp list`| Requests, in order| Declared in full  
---|---|---|---  
`legacy`| Connected| `server/discover` → `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list`| `{"elicitation": {"form": {}, "url": {}}, "roots": {"listChanged": true}}`  
`modern`| Connected| `server/discover` → `tools/list`| `{"elicitation": {"form": {}, "url": {}}, "roots": {"listChanged": true}}`  
  
  * Claude Code probes `server/discover` with revision 2026-07-28 first, and against the legacy probe falls back to `initialize` with 2025-11-25. It speaks both eras, and the vendor page names 2026-07-28 (6).
  * It declares `elicitation` (with `form` and `url`) and `roots` (with `listChanged`), and no `sampling`. That equals cells 4 and 5 and the empty sampling cell of section 2: the vendor page and the wire agree.
  * In the modern run it still sends `roots.listChanged`, although the 2026-07-28 schema defines `roots` without fields. The schema does not forbid extra fields; a server should ignore this one.
  * `claude mcp list` requested `tools/list` only. It is a health check, not a session, so the missing `resources/list` and `prompts/list` prove nothing (section 7).

**claude_code_probe.py**
    
    
     #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """Connect the real Claude Code CLI to the probe server and print what it declares.
    
    `claude mcp list` health-checks every configured server, so adding the probe and running it once records the
    client's own handshake. HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR point at a throw-away directory, so your own
    Claude Code configuration and servers are neither read nor changed. Needs the `claude` CLI on PATH; exit code 3
    when it is missing.
    Usage: claude_code_probe.py [--save FILE]   (--save writes the full records of both runs as JSON)
    """
    import argparse
    import json
    import os
    import shutil
    import subprocess
    import sys
    import tempfile
    import threading
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import client_probe_server as probe
    
    PORT = 8243
    URL = "http://127.0.0.1:%d/mcp" % PORT
    
    
    def run_era(era, env, cwd):
        records = []
        server = probe.serve(era, PORT, records.append)
        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        try:
            subprocess.run(["claude", "mcp", "add", "--transport", "http", "-s", "local", "probe", URL],
                           cwd=cwd, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
            listed = subprocess.run(["claude", "mcp", "list"], cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
            status = [line for line in listed.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("probe:")]
            subprocess.run(["claude", "mcp", "remove", "probe", "-s", "local"], cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()
            thread.join()
        return records, status[0].split(" - ")[-1] if status else "no status line"
    
    
    def main():
        ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        ap.add_argument("--save")
        args = ap.parse_args()
        if not shutil.which("claude"):
            print("claude CLI not found on PATH", file=sys.stderr)
            return 3
        version = subprocess.run(["claude", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60).stdout.strip()
        print("claude --version: %s" % version)
        saved = {"version": version}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as home, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cwd:
            env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=os.path.join(home, ".config"),
                       CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=os.path.join(home, ".claude"))
            for era in ("legacy", "modern"):
                records, status = run_era(era, env, cwd)
                saved[era] = records
                print("run: probe era=%s, claude mcp list says: %s" % (era, status))
                for record in records:
                    print(probe.summarize(record))
                first = next((r for r in records if "capabilities" in r), None)
                if first:
                    print("  declared in full: %s" % json.dumps(first["capabilities"], sort_keys=True))
        if args.save:
            Path(args.save).write_text(json.dumps(saved, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        sys.exit(main())

**Recorded output: claude_code_probe.py**
    
    
     claude --version: 2.1.292 (Claude Code)
    run: probe era=legacy, claude mcp list says: ✔ Connected
      server/discover            protocol=2026-07-28 client=claude-code/2.1.292 declares=['elicitation', 'roots']
      initialize                 protocol=2025-11-25 client=claude-code/2.1.292 declares=['elicitation', 'roots']
      notifications/initialized  protocol=2025-11-25
      tools/list                 protocol=2025-11-25
      declared in full: {"elicitation": {"form": {}, "url": {}}, "roots": {"listChanged": true}}
    run: probe era=modern, claude mcp list says: ✔ Connected
      server/discover            protocol=2026-07-28 client=claude-code/2.1.292 declares=['elicitation', 'roots']
      tools/list                 protocol=2026-07-28 client=claude-code/2.1.292 declares=['elicitation', 'roots']
      declared in full: {"elicitation": {"form": {}, "url": {}}, "roots": {"listChanged": true}}

## 7\. Reading the log

You see in the log| It means| What to do  
---|---|---  
`server/discover` with `protocol=2026-07-28`, then list calls, no `initialize`| A modern-era client talking to a modern server. Each request carries the declaration in its `_meta`| Read the declaration from every request; keep no per-connection state for it  
`server/discover` refused, then `initialize` with an older `protocol`| A legacy client, or a modern one falling back (the SDK and Claude Code both do). The declaration is made once, in `initialize`| Store it per connection at `initialize`. Do not log the refused `server/discover` as an error  
`declares` has no `sampling`| The client will not answer sampling requests| Make sampling optional: offer a path that does not call the client's model. If a request cannot be served without it, answer with `-32021` in 2026-07-28  
`elicitation` has `form` and `url`| Both modes are allowed. An empty `{}` means form only (2025-11-25)| Pick the mode from the declaration and never send one that is missing  
`roots` is declared, but you see no `roots/list` call| The declaration says the client will answer. It does not ask by itself| Ask when you need it: with a request in the legacy era, inside `inputRequests` in 2026-07-28  
Only `tools/list` was requested| Not proof that resources or prompts are unsupported: this may be a health check, or the host asks when the user does| Compare with the vendor's page (section 3) and a real session  
Requests after `initialize` carry no client name or capabilities| In the legacy era the declaration is made once per connection| Correlate by connection, not by request  
  
## 8\. Failure modes

Failure| Why it happens| Fix  
---|---|---  
The server sends sampling or elicitation without checking the declaration| The client never declared it. Both specs forbid relying on undeclared capabilities| Check `capabilities` before each such request and branch; in 2026-07-28 an unmet need is a `-32021` error  
An empty cell is read as "not supported"| The matrix records what a page says, and a page can be silent about something the product does| Treat empty as unknown and measure it with the probe  
A copied matrix goes stale| Vendors change their pages and their products| Date every cell, keep the quote, and fetch the page again before you rely on it  
A declared capability does not work in some mode| The vendor limits it: Claude Code serves elicitation "only in interactive terminal sessions" (c1)| Read the limits on the vendor's page; test the mode your users run  
One revision is assumed per client| Clients speak several: both clients in section 6 probe the modern revision first and fall back| Support both eras, or follow the compatibility matrix on the [learning path](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/learning-path/)  
Sub-capabilities are ignored| `sampling.tools`, `sampling.context` and `elicitation.url` exist only in later revisions| Test the sub-field, not only the capability  
  
## 9\. Add or re-check a row

  1. Find the vendor's own page for the feature. If it states the feature, copy the sentence exactly and note the URL and the date; if it does not, leave the cell empty.
  2. Run the probe against the client (section 5). Compare `declares` with what the page says about roots, sampling and elicitation. When they disagree, one of the two is wrong; trust the wire for what the client sends, and the vendor for what the product does with it.
  3. Write down the client's version next to the measurement.
  4. Repeat steps 1 and 2 when the client upgrades, and when the page changes.

MCP Learning Path: Choose by Role and by Spec Revision

# MCP Learning Path: Choose by Role and by Spec Revision

The shortest route through MCP is not a fixed list of chapters. It depends on two things you can decide in a minute: which role you play, and which protocol era your peers speak. The two decisions below become tables, and every stage ends with a check that you can run and that either passes or does not.

Read in this order: pick your role (section 1), pick the protocol era you build for (section 2), migrate if you already have something on an older revision (section 3), follow the stages (section 4), and come back to section 5 when something does not work.

## 1\. Pick your role

Role| You want to| Read, in this order| Run first| You are done when  
---|---|---|---|---  
Evaluating MCP| Decide whether MCP fits and what it covers| [Introduction](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/getting-started/intro/), [Architecture](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/learn/architecture/), [Server concepts](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/learn/server-concepts/)| Nothing yet| You can say which of tools, resources and prompts each of your use cases needs ([prompts, section 1](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/))  
Server developer| Build a server other people's clients can call| [Build a server](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/develop/build-server/), [Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/tools/), [Resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/), [Prompts](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/), [Best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/best-practices/)| The SDK example from "Build a server", then `lint_tools.py` against it| `lint_tools.py` (and the resources and prompts linters if you offer them) exits with code 0  
Client or host developer| Connect your application to servers you did not write| [Build a client](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/develop/build-client/), [Client best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/develop/clients/client-best-practices/), [Versioning](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning/)| A request with the protocol version in `_meta`, or `server/discover` first| An `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` makes your client retry with a version from `supported`, and a legacy server is reported, not hung on  
Integrator| Wire existing servers into a host such as an IDE or chat application| [Connect to local servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/develop/connect-local-servers/), [Connect to remote servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/develop/connect-remote-servers/), [Inspector guide](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/tools/inspector/)| `inspector_smoke.py` against the server, before the host sees it| The Inspector lists the tools you expect, and the smoke test exits with code 0  
Security or platform owner| Put servers behind authentication, a gateway or a firewall| [Authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/), [Security best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices/), [Best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/best-practices/)| `probe_http.py` against a staging endpoint| `probe_http.py` exits with code 0, and you know why each WARN is acceptable  
Publisher| List a server so that others can find and install it| [Publishing](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/registry/quickstart/), [Consuming](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/registry/registry-aggregators/)| `preflight.py` on your `server.json`| `preflight.py` exits with code 0 before you run `mcp-publisher publish`  
  
## 2\. Pick the protocol era

MCP has had five revisions. The table lists what each one added that shows up in your code; the last row is where you should start today.

Revision| What it added that you will notice| Official changelog  
---|---|---  
2024-11-05| The first revision documented here; the next changelog is written relative to it| [2025-03-26 changelog](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2025-03-26/changelog/)  
2025-03-26| An OAuth 2.1 authorization framework, Streamable HTTP replacing HTTP+SSE, JSON-RPC batching, tool annotations, audio content, the `completions` capability| [Key changes](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2025-03-26/changelog/)  
2025-06-18| Batching removed again, structured tool output, servers as OAuth resource servers with protected resource metadata, Resource Indicators (RFC 8707), elicitation, resource links in tool results, the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, `title` fields| [Key changes](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2025-06-18/changelog/)  
2025-11-25| OpenID Connect Discovery, icons, incremental scope consent, URL mode elicitation, tool calling in sampling, client ID metadata documents, experimental tasks, JSON Schema 2020-12 as the default dialect| [Key changes](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2025-11-25/changelog/)  
2026-07-28| No sessions and no `initialize` handshake: every request carries its version and capabilities. `server/discover`, `subscriptions/listen`, multi round-trip requests, a required `resultType`, caching hints, the `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers| [Key changes](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/)  
  
The 2026-07-28 revision calls versions up to 2025-11-25 **legacy** (they open a session with an `initialize` handshake) and 2026-07-28 and later **modern** (version, identity and capabilities travel in each request). An implementation that speaks both is **dual-era**. What happens when two of them meet is defined by the specification's compatibility matrix:

Client| Server| Outcome| What to do  
---|---|---|---  
Modern| Modern| Works| `server/discover` is optional. On `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`, retry with a version from `supported`  
Modern| Legacy| Fails| On stdio send `server/discover` first, so that the failure is deterministic, and show the user an actionable error  
Dual-era| Modern| Works| The client stays modern  
Dual-era| Legacy| Works| The probe fails with a non-modern error (or times out) and the client falls back to `initialize`  
Legacy| Modern| Fails| A modern-only server **SHOULD** name the versions it supports in its error to `initialize`: that message may be all a legacy client can show  
Legacy| Dual-era| Works| The server answers `initialize` and serves the client by the negotiated legacy revision  
  
Legacy against legacy works by the legacy revision and is out of scope of the 2026-07-28 text. Which era to build follows from the table:

  * **A new server whose clients you control** : modern only. It is the smaller implementation, and the clients are yours to upgrade.
  * **A server with clients you do not control** , such as hosts that still send `initialize`: dual-era. A server **MAY** implement both behaviors and serve both eras on one endpoint.
  * **A client for servers you do not control** : dual-era, because a modern client against a legacy server fails. On stdio, probe with `server/discover` and fall back on any error that is not a recognized modern error; on Streamable HTTP, attempt a modern request and read the body of a `400` before falling back. Cache the answer per server process or origin.
  * **A client for servers you control** : modern only.



## 3\. Moving from 2025-11-25 to 2026-07-28

Each row is one change from the official 2026-07-28 changelog, with what you do about it and where the site covers it.

What changed| What to do| Read  
---|---|---  
Protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header are removed; list endpoints no longer vary per connection| Stop keying state or lists on a session; keep state in your own storage or carry it in `requestState`| [Best practices, section 2](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/best-practices/)  
The `initialize` handshake is removed; every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta`| Send the `_meta` fields on every request; stop waiting for an initialization result| [Versioning](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning/)  
`server/discover` is added, and servers **MUST** implement it| Implement it; call it first only when you want the supported versions up front| [Discover](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover/)  
`subscriptions/listen` replaces the GET endpoint and `resources/subscribe`| Open one stream with the notification types you want; list again after a change| [Resources, section 4](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/)  
Multi round-trip requests replace server-initiated requests such as `roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage` and `elicitation/create`| Answer an `input_required` result and retry with `inputResponses` and `requestState`| [Multi round-trip requests](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr/)  
Every result carries a required `resultType`| Send `"complete"` for ordinary results; read it before anything else on the client| [Prompts, section 5](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
`ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required on the list results and on `resources/read`| Send `ttlMs: 0` and `"private"` if you do not know better; use `"public"` only for lists identical for all users| [Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/tools/), [Prompts, section 4](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
`Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` are required on Streamable HTTP POST requests| Send both; Base64-encode a non-ASCII `Mcp-Name`; make your gateway forward them| [Prompts, section 6](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
The error code for a missing resource changes from `-32002` to `-32602`| Return `-32602`; clients should still accept `-32002` from older servers| [Resources, section 7](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/)  
`ping`, `logging/setLevel` and `notifications/roots/list_changed` are removed| Set the log level per request in `_meta`; stop sending the removed messages| [Changelog](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/)  
Experimental tasks move out of the core protocol into an official extension| Treat tasks as an extension you negotiate through `extensions`| [Extensions](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/extensions/overview/)  
SSE stream resumability and the `Last-Event-ID` header are removed| A broken response stream loses the request: the client re-issues it| [Changelog](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/)  
  
## 4\. The path in stages

Each stage ends with something you can show. The scripts named below are the ones embedded in the pages they come from. Each exits with code 0 when no check FAILs and with code 1 when at least one does.

Stage| Do| Checkpoint| Page  
---|---|---|---  
1\. Understand| Read the architecture and the server and client concepts. Learn who controls each primitive: the user (prompts), the application (resources), the model (tools)| You can name the controller of each primitive in your design| [Architecture](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/learn/architecture/), [Prompts, section 1](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
2\. Build and run| Build a server with an official SDK, following the guide for your language| The Inspector connects, negotiates a version and lists your tools: `inspector_smoke.py` exits with code 0| [Build a server](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/2026-07-28/develop/build-server/), [Inspector guide](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/tools/inspector/)  
3\. Primitives| Define tools, resources and prompts the way their pages describe, including the failure cases| `lint_tools.py`, `lint_resources.py` and `lint_prompts.py` each exit with code 0 on your endpoint| [Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/tools/), [Resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/), [Prompts](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
4\. Remote and secure| Serve over Streamable HTTP, add authorization, check Origin, token audience and the headers| `probe_http.py` exits with code 0 against staging| [Best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/best-practices/), [Authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/)  
5\. Ship| Describe the server in `server.json`, prove ownership, publish| `preflight.py` exits with code 0| [Publishing](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/registry/quickstart/)  
6\. Stay compatible| Decide the era (section 2), test the rows of the compatibility table that apply to you| Each applicable row ends as the table says, not as a hang| [Versioning](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning/)  
  
## 5\. When something does not work

Symptom| Most likely cause| Go to  
---|---|---  
A 2026-07-28 client rejects your list result| The result lacks `resultType`, `ttlMs` or `cacheScope` (the 2025-11-25 shape)| The `list-envelope` check of the three linters; [Prompts, section 9](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
HTTP `400` with `-32020` on every request| `Mcp-Method` or `Mcp-Name` is missing, differs from the body, or a non-ASCII value was not Base64-encoded| [Prompts, section 6](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/prompts/)  
`-32022` `Unsupported protocol version`| The server does not implement the version you sent| Retry with a version from `data.supported`; [Versioning](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning/)  
A legacy client cannot connect to your new server| A modern-only server rejects `initialize`| The Legacy and Modern row of section 2; build dual-era or upgrade the client  
`resources/subscribe` answers `404` with `-32601`| The method no longer exists in 2026-07-28| Use `subscriptions/listen`; [Resources, section 4](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/)  
A missing resource answers `-32002`| The server is on 2025-11-25 or earlier| Accept both codes in the client; [Resources, section 7](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/resources/)  
The model keeps calling the wrong tool, or sends invalid arguments| The definition does not let the model recover| [Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/concepts/tools/), [Best practices, section 4](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/best-practices/)  
The server works locally and fails behind a gateway| A gateway drops or rewrites `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name` or `MCP-Protocol-Version`| `probe_http.py`; [Best practices, section 5](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs/best-practices/)  
  
## Versions and Verification

Everything above is about the 2026-07-28 revision and the four before it; the facts come from the official changelogs and the versioning page of the specification, pinned to one commit.
